content:
mona_s: Heads-up — onboarding ACME Corp's private runner inside their VPC. Installer fails during bootstrap: agent can't reach auth and model-shard endpoints. Need a minimal egress allowlist + short repro steps I can hand to their network team. Error snippets below.

eli_support: Can you paste the exact stderr / curl output? @sam_infra FYI.

mona_s: Sure — from their bastion:

```
2026-02-28T14:02:18Z agent error: GET https://models-cdn.redwood-inference.com/shards/abcd failed: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
2026-02-28T14:02:19Z agent error: POST https://auth.redwood.ai/v1/token -> 502 Bad Gateway (upstream TLS handshake failed)
```

They also ran: 
```
$ curl -v https://auth.redwood.ai/v1/token -d '{"client_id":"acme"}'
* Connected to auth.redwood.ai (10.10.10.5) port 443 (#0)
* TLSv1.2 (INSECURE) server certificate verification failed.
* Closing connection 0
```

sam_infra: Two common root causes here: split-horizon DNS (resolving to internal/private IPs) or a TLS-inspecting proxy doing MITM. Two options to advise the network team:
1) Allow TLS passthrough for our domains so the proxy doesn't intercept.
2) If interception is mandatory, add the proxy CA to the hosts' trust store so cert verification succeeds.
Also ensure internal DNS is returning public IPs for our frontends or that they allow egress to the public resolvers you want to use.

Minimal egress checklist (please open 443/80 to these hostnames; prefer hostname allowlist rather than broad CIDRs):
- auth.redwood.ai :443 (OIDC / token)
- api.redwood.ai :443 (control plane)
- models-cdn.redwood-inference.com :443 (model shard ranged GETs)
- shards-us-west2.s3.amazonaws.com :443 (S3-hosted shards — prefer VPC gateway endpoint)
- artifacts.pkg.redwood-inference.com :443 (wheels/binaries)
- telemetry.redwood.ai and telem-collector.eu.redwood.ai :443 (agent telemetry/registration)
- pypi.org and files.pythonhosted.org :443 (pip installs)
- ghcr.io and registry-1.docker.io :443 (container image pulls)
- kms.*.amazonaws.com :443 (KMS envelope key ops)
- ocsp.digicert.com and ocsp.globalsign.com :80 (OCSP stapling / cert checks)
- DNS: allow UDP/TCP 53 to your resolvers and to public resolvers (e.g., 1.1.1.1 / 8.8.8.8) if using them

jordan_p: For S3 shards we strongly recommend using a VPC Gateway Endpoint or PrivateLink so you can avoid allowing broad S3 IP ranges. Also confirm the proxy isn't rewriting SNI — this breaks cert validation. Useful tests to ask the customer to run: 
```
openssl s_client -connect auth.redwood.ai:443 -servername auth.redwood.ai -showcerts
dig +short auth.redwood.ai
curl -v --resolve auth.redwood.ai:443:3.4.5.6 https://auth.redwood.ai/v1/token
```
If `dig` returns an RFC1918 IP (10.x/172.16/192.168) that's split-horizon. If openssl shows a proxy CA in the chain, it's MITM.

eli_support: Please ask the customer to paste the above outputs. If they keep seeing an "unknown CA" or "TLS handshake failed" after adding the CA, we'll request a sanitized packet capture of the TLS ClientHello/ServerHello and a traceroute to the resolved IP.

mona_s: Sent the checklist and commands. Customer confirmed the corporate TLS proxy is doing MITM and they will attempt to add the proxy CA to the host trust store. They asked if we can give CIDRs instead because their firewall team prefers CIDR rules.

sam_infra: We avoid publishing stable CIDR blocks for our CDN/S3 endpoints. Tell them: use hostname allowlisting for auth/api/telemetry frontends. For S3 shards either allow the specific bucket endpoint (shards-us-west2.s3.amazonaws.com) or use a VPC endpoint. For package and container registries use the vendor domains listed above. Reminder: OCSP must be reachable on port 80 to ocsp.* endpoints or certificate validation will fail.

infra-bot: Created support incident INC-2026-58 and linked to SUP-9843 :ticket: (auto-note).

mona_s: Thanks all — will report back once customer confirms CA install. If they still fail we'll ask for traceroute + redacted pcap.
